The Class

Seasonal Washoku Class

Cook 5 to 6 dishes built around the Ichiju Sansai philosophy: one soup, three dishes, plus sides. Seasonal ingredients, simmered dishes, grilled dishes. Real home cooking, the way Japanese families actually eat.

Dishes you might make

Chirashi zushi Oshi zushi Nikujaga Chikuzen ni Ohitashi & more, seasonally
Duration ~2.5 hours

What to Expect

How a class unfolds

01
Meet your host
A warm welcome in Tokyo. We gather, make introductions, and set the stage for an unforgettable few hours.
02
Learn what we're making
A quick introduction to today's menu: the ingredients, the cultural story, and what makes each dish distinctly Japanese.
03
Cook together
Everyone gets hands on. You'll cook every dish yourself, with guidance and stories woven in as you go.
04
Sit down and eat
Share what you made together. Slow down, taste, and let the meal speak for itself.

Why guests choose
The Local Table Japan.

Real Japanese home cooking, guided by the principles that have shaped every family meal for over 1,200 years. You cook it, eat it. And understand it.

Real home cooking, with your host
A private kitchen space. Real Japanese home cooking. The kind that can't be replicated elsewhere.
Menus built on Go shiki 五色
White, black, red, yellow, green. Japan's five color principle, balanced into every dish you make.
Ichiju Sansai 一汁三菜
One soup, three dishes. Japan's meal framework for 1,200 years. Still how families eat today.
Small, personal, unhurried
Small groups. Everyone cooks. Just Nao, you, and the food.

Your Host

Nao

After years in a demanding career, I stepped away to return to what truly nourished me: cooking with the seasons.

In Japanese cuisine, that is not a style. It is the foundation. Every ingredient has its moment, its peak. Cooking that way brought me back to myself. That culture, that tradition, is what I want to bring to your table.
Local Guide
3 years guiding visitors through Tokyo's neighborhoods and culture
Japanese Culture
Creates content on Japanese culture and local life for inbound travel audiences
"Cooking with the season changed everything for me. I hope it does something for you too."
